breadcrumb_duplicate_page_policy_note: Duplicate or migrated pages that still represent the same current content keep materially consistent breadcrumb markup until stale copies are retired or redirected.
breadcrumb_hierarchy_scope_note: Hierarchy labels keep jurisdiction and office context legible enough that the breadcrumb does not flatten a county, city, or state election office into a generic government shell.
breadcrumb_policy_note: Breadcrumb markup mirrors a real user-followable official hierarchy rather than a decorative or stale election-cycle path.
delivery_role_note: Breadcrumb and FAQ structured data may help search systems preview official voter-information pages, but the visible page and current official help lane remain controlling.
faq_duplicate_dedup_note: If the same FAQ appears on more than one page, only one authoritative instance is marked up for FAQ rich-result eligibility.
faq_eligibility_note: FAQPage markup is limited to official government FAQ/help pages with one official answer per question and is not assumed to render merely because it is present.
faq_visibility_and_single_answer_note: Marked-up FAQ questions and answers remain visibly accessible on the page and stay synchronized with the current answer edition.
misleading_markup_prohibited_note: The office does not emit breadcrumb or FAQ structured data that contradicts visible page content, invents hierarchy, or preserves stale answers after the page changed.
public_search_feature_surface_label: Example State official voter-information breadcrumb / FAQ search-appearance policy
search_feature_boundary_note: Search-appearance markup does not replace the visible page title, page body, breadcrumb navigation, or current help/contact lane.
validation_and_rollout_note: Template and navigation changes trigger bounded revalidation using public-facing inspection tools before or immediately after rollout.
